sections.h2: Who to call about property tax
sections.html:
Two offices in Sayre share the job. The Assessor sets values, and the Treasurer collects the bill.

  • Assessor: 301 E Main St. #2, Sayre, OK 73662, phone (580) 928-3329.
  • Treasurer: (580) 928-2589, Treasurer@beckhamcountyok.gov, mail to P.O. Box 600, Sayre, OK 73662.

The Assessor does not set tax rates, adopt budgets or collect taxes. Rates come from the local taxing jurisdictions, and the Assessor's site has a property tax estimator and a school district mill rate lookup. The Treasurer collects and apportions all ad valorem taxes for the county and its subdivisions and enforces collection of delinquent taxes through tax sales.

Ask the Assessor why your value is what it is. Ask the Treasurer how much you owe and when it is due.

sections.h2: Due dates, penalties and how to pay
sections.html:
Taxes become due on November 1. You can pay the full amount or the first half by December 31, and the second half by March 31. A statement of $25 or less must be paid in full.

Beckham County property tax calendar
DateWhat happens
March 15Assessor deadline for homestead and other exemptions and for personal property renditions without penalty
October 1Assessor certifies the tax amounts to be collected
November 1Taxes first become due
Mid-NovemberCurrent statements are mailed
December 31Last day for full payment or first half before delinquency
March 31Last day for the second half
Second Monday in JuneTax resale at the Treasurer's office, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.

Penalty starts at 1.5 percent per month after December 31, and the second half starts accruing in April. Not receiving a statement does not excuse the tax (O.S. 68 section 2915). If a mortgage company escrows your taxes, the statement goes to the lender. Lender payments often arrive at the end of December and may not post until early January.

You can pay online at the Treasurer's tax roll page. Third-party charges are $1.75 for an eCheck and 2.95 percent of the tax for a card. There is also a drop box at the security desk in the courthouse lobby.

sections.h2: How the Assessor values a house
sections.html:
The Assessor estimates market value with recognized appraisal methods, then applies the state's assessment ratio to reach assessed value. Exemptions come off next, which leaves taxable value, and the millage rates apply to that figure.

The office looks at these factors:

  • Recent sales and market activity in the area.
  • Size, age, quality and condition of the house.
  • Location and neighborhood influences.
  • Construction type, additions and new building.
  • Comparable properties.

State law limits how fast taxable market value can climb in a year: 3 percent for agricultural property or a home with a homestead exemption, and 5 percent for other property. The limit resets when the property is sold or transferred. A buyer may therefore see a jump in value the year after a sale, even when the seller's bill grew slowly.

File in writing with the Assessor within 30 days of the date the Change of Value Notice was mailed. With no notice, the deadline is the first Monday in April. The state's Form 974 is the informal protest. It asks for your opinion of value and your evidence, such as a sale, comparable sales or an appraisal.

Miss the 30 days and the Assessor's value becomes final for that year. After a timely protest the Assessor must hold an informal hearing, either by phone or in person. If you are still unhappy, appeal to the county board of equalization on Form 976. All protest proceedings must finish by May 31 or the board's adjournment date.

Bring photographs, measurements, sales information or details of any correction. An appeal rarely pays off right before a closing, but a value error that persists will follow the buyer.

The homestead exemption takes $1,000 off the assessed valuation of your primary residence. You must be an Oklahoma resident living in the home by January 1. Apply at the Assessor's office or mail Form OTC 921, and file by March 15.

You do not need to renew while you still live there and the deed has not changed. When you sell, the new owner has to apply in their own name. The Assessor also holds in-person sessions for exemptions and personal property, so ask the office for the schedule.

sections.h2: Taxes and fees when a house changes hands
sections.html:
A deed worth more than $100 carries documentary stamp tax of $0.75 per $500 of consideration, leaving out liens that stay on the property. Stamps are bought when the deed goes to the county clerk, and the buyer's complete address must be on its face. A seller claiming an exemption writes the statute reference on the deed. Confirm the current rate with the clerk.

The Treasurer's mortgage tax is separate and applies to mortgages, not ordinary deeds. It runs from 2 cents to 10 cents per $100 depending on the term, plus a $10.00 certification fee per mortgage. A cash buyer pays no mortgage tax.

Delinquent property can be sold at the June resale once the county has held a tax lien for two full years. Short of that, owed taxes are usually paid from your proceeds at closing, so ask the Treasurer for a current balance before you sign.

  1. Get a payoff figure from the Treasurer at (580) 928-2589.
  2. Check whether your homestead exemption is on file so the buyer starts with an accurate record.
  3. Give the title company the payoff so it can be paid at closing.

A cash buyer can close around a tax balance, which helps when the house has fallen behind. Many sellers here hold older houses, rural parcels or inherited property, and the calendar above applies to all of them.

faqs.q: When are Beckham County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes become due November 1. You pay the full amount or first half by December 31 and the second half by March 31. Statements of $25 or less must be paid in full.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Beckham County taxes late?
faqs.a: Penalty accrues at 1.5 percent per month after December 31 until paid. Penalty on the second half begins in April.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Beckham County property value?
faqs.a: File a written protest with the Assessor within 30 days of the mailing date of your Change of Value Notice, or by the first Monday in April if no notice was sent. Form 974 is the informal protest form.

faqs.q: How much is the Beckham County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It takes $1,000 off the assessed valuation of your primary residence. You must live in the home by January 1 and file by March 15.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Beckham County house that has unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Taxes owed are normally paid from the proceeds at closing, and a cash buyer can close with a tax balance outstanding. Ask the Treasurer for the payoff amount first.
